title: That $13.99 Subscription You Forgot About Is Actually a $7,288 Decision
hook: One forgotten thirteen-dollar-a-month subscription, invested instead over twenty years at a normal market return, turns into more than seven thousand dollars.
description:
A forgotten $13.99/month subscription feels too small to matter. Left alone for 20 years it's about $3,358 out of your pocket. Invested instead at a normal 7% average return, that same $13.99 a month becomes $7,287.76. We run the real compounding math on one easy-to-ignore recurring charge.

This video uses AI-generated narration and visuals.

#Shorts #personalfinance #compoundinterest #savingmoney

segments.text: A forgotten thirteen dollar and ninety nine cent subscription. Easy to ignore -- it's less than a coffee.
Over ten years, that's one thousand six hundred seventy eight dollars, paid out a few dollars at a time.
Now instead of spending it, invest that same thirteen dollars and ninety nine cents every month, at a normal seven percent average return.
Twenty years later: seven thousand, two hundred eighty seven dollars. More than double what you would have paid out, from the same small amount.
Same thirteen dollars and ninety nine cents, either way. The only difference is what happens to it after you spend it, or don't.
That's not a reason to cancel every subscription you own. It's a reason to actually notice what the small recurring ones cost.

lines: It's about what it could have become.
